tasks.short: Plan training sessions around rooms, forklifts, instructors and shift rosters across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.

today.trigger: New hires and flex workers start, certificates (forklift, VCA, food safety) near expiry, or a manager asks for a session.
steps: Export expiring certificates and open enrolments from Studytube into Excel
Check shift rosters in AFAS and ask site supervisors who can be released
Check room, forklift and external instructor availability by mail and Outlook calendars
Book the session in Studytube and send Outlook invitations
Rebook no-shows and late cancellations by phone and mail
drudgery: Copying names between Studytube, AFAS and Excel
Chasing supervisors and instructors for dates
Rebooking after shift swaps and no-shows
today.time_sinks: Matching three-shift rosters to instructor and equipment slots per site, then redoing it when rosters change.

lenses.faster: Gathering, matching and inviting disappear; the specialist spends minutes a week reviewing the proposed plan and the conflicts list.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly job reads Studytube expiry dates, new starts in AFAS and the roster, proposes sessions inside each person's shift, and books them; the specialist only handles conflicts and external-instructor bookings that cost money.
lenses.ambitious: Book every shift worker and flex worker for renewal before the lapse, so nobody arrives at a first shift uncertified; demand would grow, since sites would ask for more short sessions if booking cost nothing.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing supervisors for release dates; the specialist gets time to sit in on sessions and improve them.
lenses.options: Little value: a single feasible plan is enough, though showing two options when an instructor is scarce helps the site manager choose.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from booking to watching a certification-coverage view per site; the specialist sets the booking rules and lead times and gains the right to release staff for training within agreed limits.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's work of registering new starters for mandatory week-one training; needs basic AFAS roster and Studytube API knowledge
Take over agency coordination of flex-worker induction slots; needs to learn the three agency portals

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with site managers in peak season about who can leave the floor, and judging when a lapse risk justifies an extra paid session.
tasks.pattern_why: Expiry dates, rosters and room capacity are structured data with rules that can be written down; no model is needed to run it.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly run after the AFAS extract refresh, plus a new starter or expiry inside the lead-time window.
steps: Read Studytube certificates and enrolments and AFAS contracts and rosters
Find people due within the lead time and slots inside their shifts
Match to room, equipment and instructor calendars and book in Studytube
Send Outlook invitations to employee and supervisor, Teams note for flex workers via agency contact
List conflicts and unbookable cases for the specialist
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves bookings that add external instructor cost and resolves every conflict; routine internal bookings go through.
in_practice.logs_to: Booking log table feeding a Power BI certification-coverage page

evidence.claim: Certificate expiry, enrolment and scheduling fit deterministic software at autonomy 4 using Studytube expiry dates and AFAS rosters.
evidence.source: Research digest, 'For the model' section (model knowledge)

evidence.claim: VCA and forklift skills are certified by outside bodies; scheduling only prepares and books learners.

risks: Roster data in AFAS lags real shift swaps, so bookings collide with actual shifts
Flex workers are not in AFAS, so they drop out unless agency data is fed in
Automatic booking that tracks individuals may count as a monitoring-capable tool needing works council consent (WOR 27(1)(l))
research_questions: Do Studytube and AFAS Profit expose APIs for enrolments and rosters at Noordhaven's licence level?
How often do rosters change after booking, per site?
Can the three staffing agencies deliver flex-worker start dates in a structured feed?
Does the OR view automatic booking based on certificate data as a consent matter?

tasks.short: Track training spend against budget and write the cost report that justifies it to finance.

today.trigger: Month close, quarterly budget review, or a question from the Controller or HR Director.
steps: Pull training cost ledger lines and supplier invoices from AFAS
Collect external course invoices and agency invoices for training hours
Map costs to sites, departments and mandatory versus optional training in Excel
Compare to budget and write a short explanation of variances
Send the report to HR Director and Controller
drudgery: Coding invoices to the right site and course by hand
Rebuilding the same Excel each month
today.time_sinks: Matching invoices to courses and people, and explaining variances that come from coding errors.

lenses.faster: Collection, mapping and the variance table run themselves; the specialist reviews outliers and writes two or three lines of explanation.
lenses.autonomous: After month close a job joins AFAS ledger lines, invoices and Studytube enrolments, codes them by site and training type, and refreshes a Power BI page; the specialist checks flagged mismatches before the report goes to the Controller.
lenses.ambitious: Report cost per certified shift worker and per new hire reaching day 90, by site, every month, so the HR Director can decide budget shifts between sites more often than once a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses invoice matching; the specialist wants more of the conversation about what the spend achieved.
lenses.options: Scenarios matter for the budget: comparing in-house forklift instructors against external providers, or seasonal flex volume, changes the decision.
lenses.altitude: The specialist moves from compiling to defending the training investment case, with cost-per-outcome figures; they gain a say in the training budget split by site.
reach: Take over the FP&A Analyst's training-budget line forecast; needs basic forecasting in Excel or Power BI
Absorb the Bookkeeper's coding of training invoices; needs AFAS cost-centre rules

tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a cost is worth it to the Controller and HR Director, and knowing which variances are real choices and which are coding noise.
tasks.pattern_why: Cost lines, budgets and enrolments are structured; mapping rules can be written once and run every month without a model.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS month close completed and the nightly extract refreshed.
steps: Pull training cost centres and invoices from AFAS and agency portals
Match invoices to Studytube enrolments and completions
Code by site, department and mandatory versus optional
Refresh Power BI budget-versus-actual and cost-per-certified-employee pages
Flag unmatched invoices and variances above threshold
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist reviews flagged items and signs off the commentary before the report goes to the Controller.
data_needed: Training cost centres and ledger lines
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset with a mapping-exceptions table

evidence.claim: Cost reports fit deterministic software at autonomy 4.
evidence.source: Research digest, 'For the model' section (model knowledge)

evidence.claim: No opened source shows a course cutting time-to-skill; baselines before launch are advised.

risks: Inconsistent cost-centre coding in AFAS makes matching unreliable
Cost-per-person views could slide into individual tracking, which needs works council consent
Agency invoices mix training hours with productive hours
research_questions: What share of training invoices today can be matched to a Studytube course automatically?
Does the Controller accept a Power BI page in place of the Excel report?
Are training costs on separate AFAS cost centres per site?

tasks.short: Build a programme that grows warehouse staff and office juniors into team leaders and supervisors.

today.trigger: Yearly talent review, a shortage of shift leaders, or an HR Business Partner request.
steps: Collect nominations from site managers and HR Business Partners
Interview candidates and managers about needs
Design the programme modules, mentors and assignments
Arrange external trainers and internal speakers
Follow participants and report progress to the HR Director
drudgery: Assembling progress overviews from scattered notes
today.time_sinks: Designing modules and gathering input from managers across three sites and three shifts.

lenses.faster: Module outlines, case material, reflection prompts and progress summaries are drafted by AI; selection, design choices and coaching stay with the specialist.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone: AI drafts material and practice scenarios on request, and every draft is approved by the specialist before use.
lenses.ambitious: Open a shift-leader track to night-shift warehouse staff and long-term flex workers, a group that is rarely nominated today; demand would grow as sites see internal promotion fill supervisor gaps.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses writing programme brochures; the specialist wants more one-to-one coaching and time on the floor spotting potential.
lenses.options: Useful: two or three programme designs (modular on-shift versus cohort off-site) change what managers will release people for.
lenses.altitude: The specialist becomes the owner of the internal succession pipeline for shift leaders, with a say in who is nominated; the work gets more expert, not less.
reach: Take over part of the HR Business Partner's succession planning for operational roles; needs talent-review facilitation skills
Feed the Recruiter's internal-mobility pipeline; needs to learn Recruitee pipeline stages

tasks.human_edge: Spotting potential in people the data misses, earning managers' trust to release them, and judging fairness of selection.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist leads design and selection; AI only speeds drafting and preparing practice material.

in_practice.trigger: Specialist starts a new cohort or redesigns a module.
steps: Specialist sets goals and target group with HR Director and site managers
AI drafts module outlines, case studies from logistics situations and feedback-practice scenarios
Specialist edits and tests with a manager
AI drafts invitations and cohort summaries from the specialist's notes
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every module and all communication; selection of participants is never made or scored by AI.
data_needed: Competence profiles for shift leader and supervisor

evidence.claim: Workday's agent drafting feedback against the SBI rubric raised write-up quality 16 points for users against 7 for non-users.
An assistant raised novices' productivity 34% in customer support.
Learners who delegate to AI scored 17% lower on mastery; those asking for explanations kept more.
Microsoft's Learning agent shows skill gaps and pathways, while HR still guides leadership development.

risks: Using AI to rank potential from learning or HR data becomes high-risk under Annex III 4(b) from 2 December 2027 and needs OR consent
Participants who let AI do reflection work learn less
Generic AI cases that do not fit warehouse reality lose credibility with team leaders
research_questions: How many shift-leader vacancies per year are filled internally today, and how many stay 90 days?
Would site managers release night-shift staff for a modular programme?
Does practising feedback with an AI scenario improve new team leaders' feedback quality at Noordhaven?

tasks.short: Make and run training on energy use, waste, recycling and fuel-efficient driving for sites and drivers.

today.trigger: A sustainability target, a customer audit or CSRD reporting request, or a new waste procedure.
steps: Gather the procedure and targets from the facility or sustainability lead
Write a short course or toolbox talk
Build it in Studytube or as a PowerPoint for shift starts
Enrol target groups and track completion
drudgery: Turning procedure documents into slides and quiz questions
today.time_sinks: Writing and adapting content for different sites, shifts and languages.

lenses.faster: Studytube AI Authoring drafts the module and quiz from the procedure PDF; the specialist edits and the facility lead checks facts.
lenses.autonomous: When a procedure in SharePoint changes, a draft update of the module is prepared for review; nothing is published without approval.
lenses.ambitious: Serve flex workers and drivers for the first time with five-minute toolbox modules per site in their own language (for example Polish or Romanian); demand would grow if per-site versions became cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rewriting slides per site; the specialist wants more time on the floor checking whether waste separation actually changed.
lenses.options: Limited: two formats (toolbox talk versus e-learning) may be tested, but the content is set by the procedure.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the sustainability learning catalogue and agrees measurable behaviour targets with facility leads before building.
reach: Support the Controller's CSRD data request with training coverage figures; needs to learn which disclosures ask for training data

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what actually happens at the dock and in the cab, and getting supervisors to back the behaviour change.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a procedure document into a draft module and quiz inside the existing Studytube workflow, and a person checks it.

in_practice.trigger: New or changed sustainability procedure uploaded to SharePoint, or a request from a facility lead.
steps: Upload the procedure to Studytube AI Authoring to draft outline, text and questions
Generate site and language variants
Specialist edits; facility or sustainability lead checks facts
Publish and enrol target groups via the scheduling job
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves content; facility lead signs off on facts before publication.
data_needed: Current procedures and targets per site
Baseline figures for waste or fuel

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outlines, scripts and questions from a title or uploaded file; authors edit.
MHR's learning team has an agent draft content and check reading level, with a person reviewing and measures agreed with the manager up front.
Fixing AI output takes a large share of AI time for desk workers.

risks: Machine translations of procedures may be wrong in ways the specialist cannot check
Completion figures are mistaken for behaviour change
Any AI tutor in the module must disclose it is AI (Art. 50)
research_questions: Which sustainability behaviours have a baseline Noordhaven can measure (waste per site, fuel per km)?
Does Studytube AI Authoring produce usable Polish and Romanian versions?
Do customers or CSRD reporting require training records on sustainability?

role.altitude: From producing courses and booking sessions to owning the competence record for 1,200 staff and flex workers, the AI-literacy (Art. 4) measures file, and the internal pipeline for shift leaders, judged on certified-on-first-shift, week-one onboarding and 90-day retention.
reach: HR Administrator: registering new starters for mandatory training
HR Business Partner: succession planning for operational leadership roles
FP&A Analyst: forecasting the training budget line
Recruiter: internal-mobility candidates for shift-leader vacancies
role.ceiling_note: Scheduling and cost reporting (about 8% of time) can shrink by more than half; design, coaching and delivery of practical safety training stay human, and works council consent plus the 2 December 2027 high-risk rules limit any use of learning data to judge people.
skills_to_grow: Writing booking and cost rules precisely enough to automate
Power BI and basic data modelling on the AFAS extract
Reviewing and correcting AI-drafted course content
EU AI Act Art. 4 and Art. 50 and WOR consent procedure
Measuring behaviour outcomes with agreed baselines
role.ambitious_version: Give every shift and flex worker a booked, multilingual, site-specific path from day one to certified and productive, and open a shift-leader track to night-shift and long-term flex staff, while keeping a defensible AI-literacy record for the whole company.
